candidate.title: DSB-Seq
candidate.scope: DSB-Seq as depicted in the assigned middle row of the Illumina poster: genomic DNA, TdT/biotinylated-dUTP end labelling, DNA isolation and random shearing, streptavidin capture, and the DNA endpoint. The matched Baranello et al. implementation clarifies the capture-to-free-DNA transition and the broad downstream Illumina library/readout interface. Adjacent BLESS, GUIDE-seq and clipped SSB-Seq rows are independent poster context, not target alternatives. No etoposide experiment, SSB-Seq workflow, kit adaptation or complete executable protocol is extracted.

features: The biological target is genomic double-strand breaks; the chemical substrate is genomic DNA with accessible ends.
Primary implementation labels high molecular weight genomic DNA after isolation.
Intentional random fragmentation has not yet been performed.

states.label: Genomic sequence reads representing the enriched break-associated DNA
features: Reads are from genomic DNA inserts, rather than from the biotin handle.
Genomic alignment localizes regions represented in the selected fraction; the drawing alone does not establish exact nucleotide break positions or complete recovery of all DSB end chemistries.

operations.label: TdT and biotinylated-dUTP
operations.description: Add biotin-containing nucleotide tails to the accessible 3-prime ends of the double-stranded genomic DNA. Input DNA becomes affinity-labelled DNA before the intentional fragmentation step.
operations.mechanism: TdT catalyses 3-prime end tailing with biotin-modified nucleotides. TdT is the catalyst and biotinylated-dUTP is a labelling reagent, not a separate workflow branch.
operations.information_effect: Covalent tail incorporation associates an affinity handle with DNA adjacent to a pre-shearing end; the genomic sequence remains the eventual location carrier.

operations.label: DNA isolation and random shearing
operations.description: Retain the source caption as one broad block: purify labelled DNA and randomly fragment it. The output is a mixture of shorter DNA pieces, some retaining the previously installed end label. In the primary implementation high molecular weight DNA was already isolated before tailing, and the deliberate fragmentation is sonication.
operations.mechanism: The paper reports sonication of biotinylated DNA; the poster does not expand the purification block.
operations.information_effect: The biotin-bearing piece retains genomic DNA adjacent to the original labelled end. Other sheared pieces do not inherit that handle; newly generated fragmentation ends are downstream of the labelling operation.

operations.label: Capture on streptavidin beads
operations.description: Select biotin-bearing DNA fragments from the sheared mixture by binding them to streptavidin-coated beads. The output differs in both composition and attachment state: an enriched, bead-associated fraction.
operations.mechanism: Biotin-streptavidin affinity binding retains the labelled fraction. No additional library preparation branch or pooling is depicted.
operations.information_effect: Enrichment transfers the original label-to-genomic-DNA association into a selected fragment population; background exclusion is a selection principle, not a claim of perfect biological specificity.

operations.label: Capture-to-DNA interface: release and biotin-tail removal (primary-source clarification)
operations.description: Resolve the condensed transition from bead capture to the rightmost DNA endpoint: release captured DNA from streptavidin complexes, remove biotinylated tails with S1 nuclease and purify the remaining genomic DNA. These actions are reported in the primary paper; they have no separate caption or reaction arrow in the supplied DSB-Seq row.
operations.mechanism: Disruption of the biotin-streptavidin complexes releases DNA; S1 nuclease removes the biotinylated tails.
operations.information_effect: The bead and label are removed, while selection history remains encoded by which genomic fragments were retained. The sequence insert, rather than the excised label, carries genomic-location information.

operations.label: Illumina sequencing and genomic readout (reported downstream interface)
operations.description: Sequence the genomic inserts in the library to produce reads that can be placed in genomic context. The paper reports Illumina Genome Analyzer sequencing and genomic alignment; no sequencing instrument or analysis block is drawn in the assigned row.
operations.information_effect: Read sequences report the genomic content of the enriched fraction and thus its distribution near labelled DNA ends. This architecture does not establish a calibrated count of all cellular DSBs or exact nucleotide break sites.

checks.rationale: Independent inspection supports the DSB-Seq-only extraction. The directly depicted genomic-DNA labelling, subsequent random shearing, and bead capture are all represented with their material routes and retained attachment states. The drawn DNA endpoint is preserved, with release and tail removal attributed explicitly to the matched primary implementation. The broad library/readout interfaces are clearly reported extensions needed to explain the sequenced carrier, rather than invented poster blocks. No independent retained branch, alternative workflow, compartment, or consequential transformation is omitted. The only unresolved visual detail is unkeyed terminal colouring; no chemical identity is asserted for it. All listed references and the sole target method are assessed at the correct evidence level.
